# Metric library: growth notes

What the metric library deliberately leaves out, so a rebuild knows these are choices, not gaps, and how each could be added later. None of them is needed for the rules in [its rules page](rules.md) to hold.

## Draft and Ready states

**Why it was left out:** A metric is usable as soon as it has a name, a unit and a direction, which is all a team needs to start. A review step before anyone can use one would slow the first weeks for little gain at Faro’s size.

**How it could grow:** Add a state to the metric (draft, ready), let goals link only to ready ones, and give whoever reviews definitions (a data owner, say) a list of drafts to approve. The rules page’s “who may” paragraph is where the new rule goes.

## Versions, with a reason for each change

**Why it was left out:** Every change is already in the change log, field by field, with who and when, which answers “what did this mean in March?” for now.

**How it could grow:** Keep each saved definition as a version with a required reason (as a goal’s plan keeps its earlier plans), show which version a goal’s numbers were read under, and let a reader compare two.

## Owner-only editing and other governance

**Why it was left out:** Owners and admins can change a metric, as with goals. Stricter rules (only the owner, or changes approved by a data steward) need roles Faro doesn’t have.

**How it could grow:** Add a steward role per metric or per source, and route changes through an ask to them (the asks model already carries who must respond).

## Dimensions an admin defines, and slices side by side

**Why it was left out:** A slice is a team or the whole company, which covers how Faro’s goals are set. Other cuts (region, product, tier) and comparing slices need data Faro doesn’t hold.

**How it could grow:** Let an admin define dimensions and their values, let a link name any of them, and add a view that lists every goal on one metric by slice, with their targets side by side.

## Suggestions and grouping look-alikes for existing goals

**Why it was left out:** Linking is by hand, by each goal’s owner. Suggesting a metric for a goal, or spotting goals that measure the same thing under different names, needs matching that is easy to get wrong in a demo.

**How it could grow:** Compare each unlinked goal’s title, unit and source with the library and suggest the closest metric; group goals whose definitions look alike and offer to link them all to one metric.

## “Metric not defined” enforcement

**Why it was left out:** A goal doesn’t have to be measured by a metric. Requiring one before a goal can be saved would block every workspace that hasn’t built its library yet.

**How it could grow:** A workspace setting that makes every number goal need a metric, a flag (like the other attention flags) on goals that have none, and a count on Home for admins.

## Numbers from the source

**Why it was left out:** A goal’s numbers come from its check-ins; the library says where each number comes from, in words.

**How it could grow:** Read each metric’s number from its source on its refresh cadence and offer it in the check-in (round 2’s MT4).
